# Solana — Colosseum resource index

Every link below is copied verbatim from Colosseum's published corpus, including its curator caveats.

### Start here

**Core resources**

- [Solana core docs](https://solana.com/docs)
  - Use the first-party map for accounts, transactions, programs, RPC, validators, payments, and tools.
- [Browser quick start](https://solana.com/docs/intro/quick-start)
  - Complete a first transaction and program exercise in Solana Playground. Its burner wallet and browser environment are for development and testing only.
- [create-solana-dapp](https://github.com/solana-foundation/create-solana-dapp)
  - Generate an app from a maintained Solana Foundation template, then inspect the selected template's client dependencies.
- [Official JavaScript and TypeScript SDKs](https://solana.com/docs/clients/official/javascript)
  - Start new TypeScript applications with @solana/kit and identify where legacy web3.js compatibility is still required.
- [Blueshift: using Solana](https://learn.blueshift.gg/en/courses/understanding-solana/using-solana)
  - Follow an active structured course. Some exercises still use legacy-compatible packages, so compare setup and client choices with current docs.

### Start Here

**Core Docs**

- [Setup Your Environment](https://solana.com/docs/intro/installation)
  - Use the maintained installation guide and confirm its displayed CLI and Anchor versions at install time. The toolchain changes quickly.

**Starter Pack**

- [Solana Playground](https://beta.solpg.io/)
  - The browser IDE is the environment used by Solana's current official quick start. Official docs limit browser-wallet use to development and testing, so teams should move durable work and secrets into a local repository.
- [Solana Stack Exchange](https://solana.stackexchange.com/)
  - The question index showed new and recently updated Solana questions at audit time. Answers vary in age and may target older SDK versions, so verify code against current official docs.
- [Solana MCP](https://mcp.solana.com/)
  - Solana's official MCP supplies current documentation retrieval plus Rust checks and autofixes for Anchor and Pinocchio. Treat generated fixes as reviewable suggestions; it does not replace tests or security review.

**Wallets + Onboarding**

- [Phantom Connect](https://docs.phantom.com/phantom-connect)
  - The maintained docs cover embedded and injected Phantom connections. App registration, SDK limits, and vendor custody/authentication choices must be evaluated before selecting it over Wallet Standard.
- [React Starter Template](https://github.com/Th3Ya0vi/phantom-embedded-react-starter)
  - The 2026-04-27 template combines Phantom SDK 2.0.2 and Kit 5.4 with legacy web3.js packages. It is useful compatibility evidence, not a clean new-app baseline, and it declares no repository license.
- [JS Template](https://github.com/Th3Ya0vi/phantom-embedded-js)
  - The template was updated 2026-04-14 and uses @phantom/browser-sdk 2.0.1 with web3.js v1. It is unofficial and declares no repository license, so inspect rather than copy or redistribute it.
- [Privy](https://docs.privy.io/basics/react/quickstart)
  - Follow the React quickstart for Solana support. Its examples use web3.js-compatible types, so Kit applications should isolate that boundary.
- [Privy Agent CLI + Sandbox](https://agents.privy.io)
  - Privy's live agent skill and sandbox document Solana wallet creation, signing, and transaction submission. It is a vendor account path and sandbox sessions are not a substitute for production key-management design.
- [Coinbase Onramp & Offramp](https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/onramp/introduction/welcome)
  - Coinbase documents Solana among supported onramp destinations. Full access, asset coverage, limits, and regional availability are account- and jurisdiction-dependent, so this is an optional fiat integration.
- [Coinbase Wallet Product Guide](https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/wallets/non-custodial-wallets/overview)
  - Compare non-custodial wallet options, then confirm the chosen product supports Solana instead of assuming support across the wallet family.

### Build programs and typed clients

**Frameworks and generation**

- [Anchor docs](https://www.anchor-lang.com/docs)
  - Build programs with account constraints, IDLs, clients, and an established test workflow. Anchor 1.x renamed its TypeScript client to @anchor-lang/core, which still depends on web3.js v1, so match the docs and package major.
- [Solana program examples](https://github.com/solana-foundation/program-examples)
  - Compare maintained native, Anchor, and Pinocchio samples without mistaking examples for deployed-app architecture.
- [Official Rust SDKs and Pinocchio](https://solana.com/docs/clients/official/rust)
  - Compare the standard program SDK with Pinocchio's lower-level, zero-dependency path before accepting its added validation burden.
- [Codama](https://github.com/codama-idl/codama)
  - Generate Kit-compatible TypeScript clients and documentation from Codama or converted Anchor IDLs.

### Test at the right layer

**Test and review tools**

- [LiteSVM](https://solana.com/docs/tools/litesvm)
  - Run fast in-process transaction and program tests from Rust, TypeScript, or Python.
- [Mollusk](https://solana.com/docs/programs/testing/mollusk)
  - Use a minified SVM for precise Rust instruction-level tests with explicit accounts and checks.
- [Surfpool](https://solana.com/docs/tools/surfpool)
  - Run RPC-level and integration workflows with a test-validator-compatible local network and just-in-time account loading.
- [Blueshift program security](https://learn.blueshift.gg/en/courses/program-security/introduction)
  - Practice signer, ownership, account-initialization, PDA, and CPI failure modes before review.

### Ship the application

**Product integration**

- [Solana frontend guides](https://solana.com/docs/frontend)
  - Connect wallets with Wallet Standard and Kit plugins, with a documented bridge for legacy web3.js dependencies.
- [Solana RPC methods](https://solana.com/docs/rpc)
  - Use the authoritative request, response, commitment, and subscription reference for application data access.
- [Solana Actions and Blinks](https://solana.com/docs/tools/actions)
  - Expose shareable transactions when distribution fits the product. The current @solana/actions line still depends on web3.js v1, so isolate it from a Kit-first client.
- [Solana payments](https://solana.com/docs/payments)
  - Choose among payment links, direct transfers, and agentic x402 flows using the current first-party payment map.
- [Solana Mobile developer docs](https://docs.solanamobile.com/)
  - Add Mobile Wallet Adapter and mobile dApp support after confirming Android and native-platform constraints.

### Tokens and permissions

**Token features and permissions**

- [Token Extensions](https://solana.com/docs/tokens/extensions)
  - Choose Token-2022 mint and account features from the official extension map. Most extensions must be selected during initialization, and some combinations are incompatible.
- [Permissioned tokens with Token ACL](https://solana.com/docs/tokenization/token-acl)
  - Implement sRFC37 permissioned transfers with the Token ACL program and pluggable gates. Its ABL gate is a reference implementation; production use requires security audits, key management, regulatory review, and legal consultation.

### Payments + Commerce

**Solana payment architecture**

- [Payment Channels](https://solana.com/payment-channels)
  - Implement repeated payments with off-chain signed updates and onchain open and settle transactions. Treat current benchmark and partner claims as launch data, not guarantees.
- [Subscriptions and Allowances](https://solana.com/docs/payments/subscriptions/overview)
  - Use Solana's shared subscriptions program for fixed or recurring delegation with documented program IDs and audit history. Pullers can transfer within an active authorization, so users and applications must enforce caps, expiry, revocation, and token-account delegation.
- [Index Solana payments](https://solana.com/docs/payments/accept-payments/indexing)
  - Design production payment ingestion with persistent streaming, historical access, and instruction parsing when RPC polling is not enough. The guide uses provider-backed gRPC and raw decoding, so plan the supporting infrastructure.

**Swig Smart Wallets**

- [TypeScript SDK](https://github.com/anagrambuild/swig-ts)
  - The Swig repository was updated 2026-08-18 and contains separate Kit and classic web3.js packages and examples. It is an active protocol SDK, not a general Solana TypeScript client.
- [Developer Portal](https://dashboard.onswig.com/)
  - The live portal is an authenticated Swig developer surface. Its public shell verifies the destination, but provisioning and post-login behavior could not be inspected without an account; list it only beside the public Swig docs.

### Agents + Tokenization

**General Agent Tooling**

- [Solana Agent Skills](https://solana.com/skills)
  - The official skills index includes Foundation-maintained skills and labels community contributions separately. It reinforces the current Kit and LiteSVM/Mollusk/Surfpool testing path; community skills are not Solana endorsements.
- [Coinbase Agentic Wallet Skills](https://github.com/coinbase/agentic-wallet-skills)
  - Use the SOL and USDC balance and transfer workflows on Solana. Trading and onchain query coverage is narrower or EVM-specific.
- [Coinbase x402](https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/x402/welcome)
  - The current x402 overview explicitly documents Solana alongside Base. Keep as protocol/vendor context, then use Solana's own x402 guide for chain-specific implementation.
- [x402 MCP Server](https://solana.com/docs/payments/agentic-payments/intro-to-x402)
  - Use Solana's chain-specific x402 guide for agent payments. The Coinbase buyer MCP path that this replaces is EVM-oriented.
- [PAY.SH](https://github.com/solana-foundation/pay)
  - Use the Solana Foundation CLI to access x402 or MPP services while a local wallet authorizes each payment. Review each request and keep wallet policy explicit.
- [LI.FI Agent Skills](https://github.com/lifinance/lifi-agent-skills)
  - The repository was updated 2026-06-10 and explicitly covers Solana among many chains. Keep only for cross-chain agent routing; it returns workflows/transactions that still require wallet policy and validation.
- [LI.FI MCP Server](https://docs.li.fi/mcp-server/overview)
  - The live MCP docs cover route discovery and unsigned transaction construction across Solana and other chains. The public service is rate-limited and does not remove wallet signing or transaction validation responsibilities.
- [Vanish Core API](https://core.vanish.trade/start/introduction)
  - This Solana transaction API requires onboarding and an API key. Its latency, routing, compliance, and security claims are vendor claims, not independent benchmarks.
- [Agentic Market](https://agentic.market/)
  - The live catalog exposes paid, x402-discoverable services and includes Solana among its network labels. Keep only as an optional discovery directory: listings, capability claims, and prices are provider-supplied and can change independently of the catalog.

### Privacy + Confidential Compute

- [Arcium Documentation](https://docs.arcium.com/)
  - Arcium's maintained documentation explains its encrypted-computation network and Solana integration. The technology adds a distinct compiler, network, and threat model and is optional for apps that truly require confidential computation.
- [Arcium Developer Docs](https://docs.arcium.com/developers)
  - This developer section supplies the actionable Arcis and Anchor-compatible build path, distinct from the conceptual docs home. Builders still need to validate network availability and security assumptions for their use case.
- [Confidential Balances](https://solana.com/docs/tokens/extensions/confidential-transfer)
  - Hide transfer amounts and confidential balances with Token-2022 confidential transfers. Addresses, mints, and owners remain public; both accounts need the extension, stock solana-test-validator lacks the proof program, transfers may require several transactions, and Rust and JavaScript clients differ.
